name: Petosiris tomb strap-powered lathe
description: A tomb scene shows two woodworkers using a strap-driven lathe to turn a long workpiece.

date.label: Around 300 BCE
date.basis: The date applies to this documented case, not to the worldwide origin of the capability.

events.statement: A tomb scene dated around 300 BCE depicts a strap-powered lathe and two workers.

evidence.supports: A tomb scene dated around 300 BCE depicts a strap-powered lathe and two workers.
The chapter identifies Petosiris’s tomb as the source of a wood-turning scene dated about 300 BCE.

contributions.group: Egyptian woodworkers depicted in the tomb

evidence.supports: A tomb scene dated around 300 BCE depicts a strap-powered lathe and two workers.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest researched operational or depicted case for this record, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: A representation, not a surviving working lathe or a date for the invention of turning. The date is approximate.

research.note: Independent review checked both the Morris discussion and the Egypt woodworking chapter; the depiction and approximate date do not establish invention.
